title: 507. The French Revolution: The Marseillaise, Song of War (Part 5)

sentences.en: Allons, enfants de la patrie, le jour de croix est l'arrivée de la tyrannie.
sentences.zh: 前进，祖国之子，暴政的十字架之日已经降临。

sentences.zh: 血腥的旗帜已经升起，血腥的旗帜已经升起。

sentences.en: Entendez-vous dans les campagnes guérir ces féroces soldats
sentences.zh: 你们可曾听到乡间传来这些凶残士兵的狂吼

sentences.en: qui viennent jusque dans vos bras égorger vos fils, vos compagnies.

sentences.en: So that was our producer, Theo Young-Smith.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的制作人西奥·杨-史密斯。

sentences.en: They were his dulcet tones.
sentences.zh: 这是他那甜美的歌声。

sentences.en: He was singing La Marseillaise, the song par excellence of the French Revolution, or at least the one French Revolutionary song that everybody now remembers.
sentences.zh: 他唱的是《马赛曲》，法国大革命中最典型的歌曲，或者至少是现在人人都记得的那首法国大革命歌曲。

sentences.en: So, Tom, that was adopted as the official anthem of the French Republic in 1795, but Napoleon didn't like it.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这首歌在1795年被采纳为法兰西共和国的官方国歌，但拿破仑并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: He didn't.
sentences.zh: 他确实不喜欢。

sentences.en: He kind of pushed it back to the margins.
sentences.zh: 他有点把它边缘化了。

sentences.en: And then after the revolution, after Napoleon, Louis XVI's brothers,
sentences.zh: 然后在大革命之后，在拿破仑之后，路易十六的兄弟们

sentences.en: Louis XVIII and Charles X, they come back.
sentences.zh: 路易十八和查理十世复辟了。

sentences.en: They obviously hate it, so they ban it completely.
sentences.zh: 他们显然很讨厌这首歌，所以彻底把它禁了。

sentences.en: But the Marseillaise is never forgotten, and it ends up as the national anthem of France.
sentences.zh: 但《马赛曲》从未被遗忘，最终它还是成了法国的国歌。

sentences.en: Theo sings it all the time as a proud Frenchman.
sentences.zh: 西奥作为骄傲的法国人，无时无刻不在唱它。

sentences.en: Would you, I mean, you are John Bull incarnate, but would you agree that it's the greatest, the most thrilling national anthem ever written?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是约翰·牛顿式的英国人化身，但你是否同意它是史上最伟大、最激动人心的国歌？

sentences.en: I mean, the most stirring?
sentences.zh: 我是说，最让人热血沸腾的？

sentences.en: Well, I saw you'd written this, and this is the sort of slack and lazy thing that people who know only two national anthems say.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我看到你写了这个，这正是那种只知道两首国歌的人才会说的偷懒又荒谬的话。

sentences.en: So, they know their own, and they know one or two others.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们只知道自己的国歌，顶多再知道一两首别的。

sentences.en: If they're American, they say it's the American one.
sentences.zh: 如果是美国人，他们会说是美国的国歌。

sentences.en: If they're British, a particular kind of Britain, they say it's the French national anthem.
sentences.zh: 如果是英国人，某种特定类型的英国人，他们会说是法国国歌。

sentences.en: But actually, people who know a lot about national anthems know that the best national anthem by far, so our assistant producer, Aaliyah, will back me up on this,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，对国歌了解很多的人都知道，迄今为止最好的国歌——我们的助理制作人阿莉娅会支持我的说法——

sentences.en: is the anthem of the German Democratic Republic.
sentences.zh: 是德意志民主共和国的国歌。

sentences.en: Auf er standen aus Ruhinen, the anthem of East Germany, which was an absolute banger, and unquestionably the greatest national anthem ever written.
sentences.zh: 《从废墟中崛起》，东德的国歌，那真是一首绝对的神曲，毫无疑问是史上写得最伟大的国歌。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, for those of us who aren't familiar with it, would you like to sing it for us?
sentences.zh: 好了，多米尼克，对于我们这些不太熟悉它的人，你想为我们唱一段吗？

sentences.en: And perhaps-
sentences.zh: 也许——

sentences.en: No?
sentences.zh: 不唱？

sentences.en: No, I wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 不，我才不唱。

sentences.en: You're clearly afraid to pitch it up against the A's magnificent singing.
sentences.zh: 你显然是不敢跟阿莉娅那美妙的歌声一较高下。

sentences.en: No, I just don't want to look like an absolute fool.
sentences.zh: 不，我只是不想让自己看起来像个彻头彻尾的傻瓜。

sentences.en: Ah, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 啊，我不觉得会这样。

sentences.en: Because obviously, as an Englishman, my soul doesn't stir with patriotic fervor when I hear the Marseillais,
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，作为一个英国人，当我听到《马赛曲》时，我的灵魂并不会涌起爱国热情，

sentences.en: except in Casablanca, that brilliant scene where-
sentences.zh: 除了在《卡萨布兰卡》里，那个精彩的场景——

sentences.en: Yeah, they will stand up and-
sentences.zh: 对，他们会站起来——

sentences.en: The Germans are sat around the piano.
sentences.zh: 德国人围坐在钢琴旁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then Humphrey Bogart agrees that they can strike up the Marseillais, and it's sung with such fervor.
sentences.zh: 然后亨弗莱·鲍加同意他们奏响《马赛曲》，大家唱得群情激昂。

sentences.en: Yeah, you love that.
sentences.zh: 对，你很喜欢那个。

sentences.en: And you are, yeah, identifying with this, and it's very, very stirring.
sentences.zh: 而且你，是的，你对这种情感感同身受，非常非常激动人心。

sentences.en: However, I mean, it is worth mentioning,
sentences.zh: 不过，我的意思是，这确实值得一提，

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But those who haven't looked closely at the lyrics, that they are incredibly martial.
sentences.zh: 那些没有仔细研究过歌词的人会发现，歌词极其好战。

sentences.en: Yeah, the bloody standard.
sentences.zh: 没错，血腥的旗帜。

sentences.en: Yes, I mean, it's kind of blood everywhere.
sentences.zh: 是的，到处都是血淋淋的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it is summoning the enfants de la patrie, the children of the fatherland, to action.
sentences.zh: 它在召唤祖国的孩子们行动起来。

sentences.en: In that first verse that Theo sung so beautifully,
sentences.zh: 在西奥刚刚优美演唱的第一段里，

sentences.en: France is menaced by ferocious soldiers who were marching beneath this banner of tyranny, which has been steeped in blood.
sentences.zh: 法国正受到凶残士兵的威胁，他们踏着浸透鲜血的暴政旗帜行进。

sentences.en: And they're coming to rip out the throats of patriotic Frenchmen's sons and wives.
sentences.zh: 他们来是要割断爱国法国人儿子和妻子的喉咙。

sentences.en: And so this great summons to arm citizens, form your battalions, let's march, let's march, and irrigate the soil with a tainted blood.
sentences.zh: 因此这是一场伟大的号召：公民们拿起武器，组成方阵，前进，前进，让污浊的鲜血灌溉土地。

sentences.en: And the tainted blood is the blood of the tyrants and their armies.
sentences.zh: 而这污浊的鲜血就是暴君及其军队的血。

sentences.en: That tells you when it's written.
sentences.zh: 这告诉你它是何时被写出来的。

sentences.en: So war has been declared, but it also tells you about the mood of the time.
sentences.zh: 当时战争已经爆发，但也反映了当时的时代情绪。

sentences.en: So we've talked a fair bit about the sort of paranoia, sense of conspiracy, sense of taint and impurity, invading the virtuous body of the French Republic.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论了不少关于偏执、阴谋论的感觉，以及污染和不洁感侵入法兰西共和国纯洁躯体的氛围。

sentences.en: But tell us a little bit more, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，跟我们多讲讲吧。

sentences.en: I know you've done some digging into this.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在这方面做了一些研究。

sentences.en: How it comes to be written and who by?
sentences.zh: 这首歌是怎么被写出来的？是谁写的？

sentences.en: Well, it's written at a time when France is still a monarchy, just about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它写于法国勉强还维持君主制的时期。

sentences.en: So it's written on the 25th of April, 1792.
sentences.zh: 它写于1792年4月25日。

sentences.en: And that's five days after France has declared war on Austria.
sentences.zh: 那是在法国对奥地利宣战的五天后。

sentences.en: And officers in Strasbourg, who are kind of pretty much on the front line, there's a dinner, a public dinner.
sentences.zh: 斯特拉斯堡的军官们几乎就身处前线，当时有一场晚宴，一场公开晚宴。

sentences.en: And it's hosted by the mayor of Strasbourg, who's a man called Philippe Dietrich.
sentences.zh: 由斯特拉斯堡市长菲利普·迪特里希主持。

sentences.en: And in one sense, he is the absolute embodiment of the intellectual revolution, the Enlightenment-infused revolution.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，他绝对是知识革命、启蒙思想革命的化身。

sentences.en: So he's a Protestant.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一名新教徒。

sentences.en: He is a distinguished scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位杰出的科学家。

sentences.en: He's a chemiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一名化学家。

sentences.en: He's a geologiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一名地质学家。

sentences.en: He loves his Enlightenment ideals.
sentences.zh: 他热爱启蒙运动的理想。

sentences.en: He sounds such a bore.
sentences.zh: 听起来真是个无趣的家伙。

sentences.en: And he's a Freemason.
sentences.zh: 他还是个共济会员。

sentences.en: Yeah, total bore.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是个无趣的人。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 你接着说。

sentences.en: But what makes it intriguing is that he is simultaneously the epitome of everything that the revolution is opposed to, because he is an ironmaster and an industrialiSt.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，他同时又是革命所反对的一切事物的缩影，因为他是一个炼铁厂主和实业家。

sentences.en: Now, I do like an ironmaster.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢炼铁厂主的。

sentences.en: I know you do.
sentences.zh: 我知道你喜欢。

sentences.en: And his forges are being powered by all the timber and the wood that he's been harvesting, and which the poor can no longer use to keep their pots boiling.
sentences.zh: 他的锻炉所需的动力全靠他砍伐的木材，而穷人们却再也买不起这些木柴来煮饭了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so they're all starving.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都在挨饿。

sentences.en: So he's a figure of sinister wealth, and he's actually a former aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 因此他是一个带着阴暗财富色彩的人物，而且他其实是个前贵族。

sentences.en: So he was the Baron de Dietrich.
sentences.zh: 他曾是迪特里希男爵。

sentences.en: So he embraces all the contradictions and ambivalences of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以他集革命的所有矛盾与矛盾心理于一身。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising that he should be keen on reinvention, the kind of reinvention that France itself in this period is having to undergo, the process of going from a monarchy
sentences.zh: 他不热衷于重塑才怪呢，就像这一时期的法国本身正在经历的重塑一样，从一个君主制国家转变为

sentences.en: to a republic.
sentences.zh: 一个共和国的过程。

sentences.en: And it's, of course, that they are on the frontier of a country at war.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们正处于一个处于战争状态的国家的边境上。

sentences.en: And so at dinner, the toasts are offered exactly the kind that you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 所以在晚宴上，大家祝酒的都是你可以想象的那种内容。

sentences.en: So to the Atri, to Liberty, to the ruin of tyrants, to the fertilizing of the soil with their blood and the blood of tyrants, all of that.
sentences.zh: 为了祖国，为了自由，为了暴君的灭亡，用他们的血和暴君的血来滋润土地，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Dietrich, he finds all the words of these toasts stirring, and he comments to the table, to the assembled officers, how tragic it is that all the marching songs that the French
sentences.zh: 迪特里希觉得这些祝酒词非常振奋人心，他对餐桌上的在座军官们感叹，法国军队

sentences.en: army have are rife with feudalism and superstition that they derive from the Ancien Régime.
sentences.zh: 所有的进行曲都充斥着封建主义和迷信，都承袭自旧制度，这实在是太可悲了。

sentences.en: And he wishes that there was a marching song that would be appropriate to the new French army, an army of patriots and citizens.
sentences.zh: 他希望有一首适合新法兰西军队的进行曲，一支由爱国者和公民组成的军队。

sentences.en: And it so happens that at that dinner, there is a captain called Roger de Lille, and he is almost a kind of mini Dietrich.
sentences.zh: 碰巧在那场晚宴上，有一位名叫鲁热·德·利尔的队长，他简直就是个微缩版的迪特里希。

sentences.en: He's a man of science.
sentences.zh: 他是一个懂科学的人。

sentences.en: He's an engineer.
sentences.zh: 他是一名工程师。

sentences.en: He's a Freemason.
sentences.zh: 他是一名共济会员。

sentences.en: But he's also a part-time composer.
sentences.zh: 但他也是个业余作曲家。

sentences.en: So he spent quite a lot of time in Paris rustling up various forgettable songs that he's trying to kind of flog to theatres and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以他花了不少时间在巴黎创作各种转瞬即逝的歌曲，试图把它们推销给剧院之类的地方。

sentences.en: But that night, the muse descends on him, and he's inspired by Dietrich's suggestion.
sentences.zh: 但就在那天晚上，灵感女神降临在他身上，迪特里希的提议启发了他。

sentences.en: He goes back to his quarters, and he spends all night writing a song that he very catchily calls the song of the army of the Rhine.
sentences.zh: 他回到住处，整晚都在写一首歌，并给它取了一个非常抓耳的名字：《莱茵军战歌》。

sentences.en: And I think that if that had stayed its title, maybe it wouldn't be as successful as it proves to be.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果当时一直叫这个名字，它可能不会取得后来的巨大成功。

sentences.en: And the next morning, he goes to the Dietrich, and he gives it to Dietrich himself, who's very, very taken with it, in Dietrich's musical.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，他去找迪特里希，把它交给了迪特里希本人，迪特里希的音乐造诣很高，对此非常非常着迷。

sentences.en: And his wife sits down at the piano, plays the chords, and Dietrich bellows it out.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子在钢琴前坐下，弹奏起和弦，迪特里希大声唱了起来。

sentences.en: And they all say, this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，这太棒了。

sentences.en: This is exactly what we need.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们需要的。

sentences.en: And so Madame Dietrich scores it for a military band, and the band strikes up.
sentences.zh: 于是迪特里希夫人为军乐队编了曲，乐队开始演奏。

sentences.en: And it's kind of literally a revelation, because to quote David Andres in his wonderful book on the terror, he describes it as an almost millennial sense of drama.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一个启示，用大卫·安德烈在他关于恐怖统治的精彩著作中的话来形容，他将其描述为一种近乎千禧年般的戏剧感。

sentences.en: And there is that sense, I think, in which it's a kind of secular dies irae.
sentences.zh: 我认为，确实有一种世俗版《最后的审判》的感觉。

sentences.en: Dies irae, the great medieval account of souls being brought before the throne of God to be
sentences.zh: 《最后的审判》（Dies irae），中世纪关于灵魂在屠杀、混乱和流血中被带到上帝宝座前接受

sentences.en: judged amid slaughter and chaos and bloodshed, and the lamb, the sheep, and the goats are separated out.
sentences.zh: 审判的伟大描写，羔羊、绵羊和山羊在其中被分开。

sentences.en: And this essentially is what is happening in the drama of what will come to be called the
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是后来被称为《马赛曲》的

sentences.en: Marseilles.
sentences.zh: 音乐所展现的戏剧性中所发生的事情。

sentences.en: Well, it has that apocalyptic sense, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，它确实有一种末日般的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That is so common in the political culture at this point, so 1792.
sentences.zh: 这在当时的政治文化中非常普遍，也就是1792年。

sentences.en: I read with great relish that the Marseilles, the music is probably not exactly plagiarized, but it's derivative.
sentences.zh: 我津津有味地读到，《马赛曲》的音乐可能不完全是抄袭，但它是衍生出来的。

sentences.en: So there are various antecedents.
sentences.zh: 所以它有各种前身。

sentences.en: There was an Italian composer called Viotti.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫维奥蒂的意大利作曲家。

sentences.en: There was an oratoria by somebody called Grison.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫格里松的人写过清唱剧。

sentences.en: And Mozart, Mozart Piano Concerto No.
sentences.zh: 还有莫扎特，莫扎特的第25号钢琴协奏曲，

sentences.en: 25, apparently, yes.
sentences.zh: 显然是的，协奏曲。

sentences.en: Disturbingly similar, Tom.
sentences.zh: 令人不安的相似，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, remember that De Lille has come to Strasbourg from Paris, where he's been stationed, and he's been hawking his stuff around all the concert halls and theatres.
sentences.zh: 好吧，记住德·利尔是从他驻扎的巴黎来到斯特拉斯堡的，他一直在各大音乐厅和剧院兜售他的作品。

sentences.en: He's got a knockoff tune that he's trying to pass off to Dietrich.
sentences.zh: 他有一首山寨曲调，正试图糊弄迪特里希。

sentences.en: I guess in the way that minor composers, I gather, are often more prone to being influenced by things that they've heard, perhaps the very greatest composers.
sentences.zh: 我想，正如我所了解的那样，小作曲家往往比伟大的作曲更容易受到他们听过的事物的影响。

sentences.en: He's clearly not a very great composer, but it wouldn't be surprising that he might kind of perhaps unconsciously plagiarize certain tunes that he's heard.
sentences.zh: 他显然不是一个非常伟大的作曲家，所以他或许会在无意中抄袭了某些他听过的曲调，这也并不奇怪。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, that's how musical composition works.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，音乐创作就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: But the bottom line is, it starts to kind of go viral because soldiers from Strasbourg, whenever, you know, they, for various reasons, they might be going back into the heartlands
sentences.zh: 但底线是，它开始像病毒一样传播开来，因为来自斯特拉斯堡的士兵，无论出于什么原因，当他们由于各种原因返回法国

sentences.en: of France, and they take it with them.
sentences.zh: 腹地时，他们把这首歌带了回去。

sentences.en: They start kind of singing it.
sentences.zh: 他们开始唱起这首歌。

sentences.en: And one of the soldiers who does this is going to Montpellier in the south of France.
sentences.zh: 其中一个这样做的士兵正前往法国南部的蒙彼利埃。

sentences.en: And there, on the 17th of June, a doctor by the name of François Mireur, here's it being sung by a soldier who's come from Strasbourg.
sentences.zh: 在那里，6月17日，一个名叫弗朗索瓦·米勒的医生听到一个从斯特拉斯堡来的士兵在唱这首歌。

sentences.en: And he immediately recognizes it as something stirring, as something patriotic.
sentences.zh: 他立刻意识到这是一首激动人心、充满爱国主义的歌曲。

sentences.en: And he finds himself humming it and then singing it.
sentences.zh: 他发现自己不由自主地哼唱起来，接着唱出了声。

sentences.en: He gets the lyrics.
sentences.zh: 他拿到了歌词。

sentences.en: And five days later, he is going to a meeting at the Jacobin headquarters in Marseille.
sentences.zh: 五天后，他去参加马赛雅各宾党总部的会议。

sentences.zh: 法国革命者赞赏这段罗马历史时期，显然是在追随

sentences.en: in the footsteps of the American revolutionaries who had cast their expulsion of a king as something redolent of the spirit of Brutus and Horatius.
sentences.zh: 美国革命者的脚步，美国革命者将他们驱逐国王的行为描绘成充满布鲁图斯和贺拉斯精神的事情。

sentences.en: And it's telling, I think, that even in the very earliest days of the revolution, long before anyone is really considering getting rid of the monarchy, you do have radicals.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这说明了即使在革命的最早期，早在真正考虑废除君主制之前，你就已经有了激进分子。

sentences.en: Desmoulins would be a classic example.
sentences.zh: 德穆兰就是一个典型的例子。

sentences.en: He's doing this all the time.
sentences.zh: 他一直在这样做。

sentences.en: Who are comparing themselves to Brutus.
sentences.zh: 他们把自己比作布鲁图斯。

sentences.en: And there are two Brutuses in the history of the Republic.
sentences.zh: 共和国历史上其实有两个布鲁图斯。

sentences.en: There is the Brutus who leads the overthrow of the monarchy and the establishment of the
sentences.zh: 一个是领导推翻君主制和建立

sentences.en: Republic.
sentences.zh: 共和国的布鲁图斯。

sentences.en: But there is also, of course, the Brutus who is descended from the first Brutus who murders
sentences.zh: 但当然，还有另一个布鲁图斯，他是第一个布鲁图斯的后代，谋杀了

sentences.en: Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 尤利乌斯·凯撒。

sentences.en: And Julius Caesar is a product of the Republic who aspires to overthrow the Republic.
sentences.zh: 而尤利乌斯·凯撒是共和国的产物，却渴望推翻共和国。

sentences.en: The Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑。

sentences.en: So Napoleon, yes, but also all these shadowy figures that true revolutionaries are anxious about hiding behind the mask of patriotism.
sentences.zh: 所以是拿破仑，是的，还有所有这些让真正的革命者感到焦虑的隐秘人物，他们藏在爱国主义的面具后面。

sentences.en: So if you're playing Marat or Robespierre or whoever, denouncing frauds, counter-revolutionaries,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你扮演马拉、罗伯斯庇尔或任何人，谴责骗子、反革命分子，

sentences.en: you can do so as a Brutus, as a patriot committed to the defense of your country against a tyrant.
sentences.zh: 你就可以作为一个布鲁图斯、一个致力于保卫国家免受暴君侵害的爱国者来这样做。

sentences.en: What was the thing we talked about the other day?
sentences.zh: 我们前几天谈论的是什么来着？

sentences.en: It was Cicero who exposed the Catiline conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 是西塞罗揭露了喀提林阴谋。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That's the big thing that Cicero...
sentences.zh: 那是西塞罗的重大事迹……

sentences.en: And they're obsessed with Cicero, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们对西塞罗着迷，不是吗？

sentences.en: Haven't they all studied Cicero's speeches and things at school?
sentences.zh: 他们不都在学校里学习过西塞罗的演讲之类的东西吗？

sentences.en: Desmoulins.
sentences.zh: 德穆兰。

sentences.en: And actually, you mentioned Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 其实，你提到了罗伯斯庇尔。

sentences.en: So I found this quote.
sentences.zh: 我找到了这段引语。

sentences.en: There's a woman called Rosalie Julien, who's a Jacquemin sympathizer.
sentences.zh: 有个叫罗莎莉·朱利安的女人，她是雅各宾派的同情者。

sentences.en: And her diaries and letters are always cited by all historians of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 她的日记和书信总是被所有革命史学家引用。

sentences.en: She wrote of Robespierre, you'd enjoy this, Tom, that he is, quote, a man who was devoted to the public with the generosity of the greatest men of antiquity.
sentences.zh: 她写罗伯斯庇尔时说——汤姆你会喜欢这个的——说他“是一个以古代最伟大人物的慷慨献身于公众的人”。

sentences.en: This Robespierre is a real Roman.
sentences.zh: 这个罗伯斯庇尔是个真正的罗马人。

sentences.en: I mean, there could be no higher praise.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，再也没有比这更高的赞誉了。

sentences.en: You've talked to Cicero and Timothy Tackett in his great book on the coming of the terror.
sentences.zh: 你跟蒂莫西·塔凯特聊过，他在那本关于恐怖统治来临的伟大著作中。

sentences.en: I mean, he quotes this amazing statistic that in speeches and newspapers during the revolution,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他引用了一个惊人的统计数据：在革命期间的演讲和报纸中，

sentences.en: Cicero would be cited 10 times more frequently than the contemporary philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 西塞罗被引用的频率是当代哲学家让-雅克·卢梭的10倍之多。

sentences.en: So you think of all the books and articles and essays that have been written about the influence of Rousseau on the revolution, but Cicero is being quoted 10 times more.
sentences.zh: 所以，想想看，那些关于卢梭对大革命影响的书籍、文章和随笔有那么多，但西塞罗被引用的次数是前者的十倍。

sentences.en: Yeah, I love that.
sentences.zh: 对，我很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: Its influence is obviously, in one sense, elite.
sentences.zh: 它的影响显然在某种意义上是精英式的。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, I was about to ask that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，我正想问这个。

sentences.en: Most people don't go to school for a long period of time and they don't study classics.
sentences.zh: 大多数人没有接受过长期的教育，他们也不研究古典文学。

sentences.en: To most people in France, this is just a mad babble.
sentences.zh: 对法国的大多数人来说，这只是一片疯狂的胡言乱语。

sentences.en: I think it's kind of in the way that people might quote Darwin or Freud or Marx today without having read any of them.
sentences.zh: 我想这有点像今天的人们可能会引用达尔文、弗洛伊德或马克思，却并没有读过他们的任何著作。

sentences.en: You have a vague sense.
sentences.zh: 你有一种模糊的概念。

sentences.en: We would never do that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会那样做，汤姆。

sentences.en: It has been known that people might drop these names without having read them, right?
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，人们可能会在没读过的情况下顺口说出这些名字，对吧？

sentences.en: It's that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种情况。

sentences.en: But I think it's also, it becomes kind of the mood music.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得，它在某种程度上变成了背景音乐。

sentences.en: It becomes actually the coloring, literally the coloring, because this sense of what it is to be a Roman is fostered above all, I think, by someone that you've already mentioned,
sentences.zh: 它实际上变成了色彩，字面意义上的色彩，因为这种“身为罗马人”的感觉，我认为，主要是由你刚刚提到的一位人物所培育的，

sentences.en: the great artist, Jacques-Louis David, who is a painter who's obsessed by Rome.
sentences.zh: 伟大的艺术家雅克-路易·大卫，他是一位痴迷于罗马的画家。

sentences.en: And his paintings are austere and self-consciously impregnated with a sense of the nobility of the early age of the Roman Republic.
sentences.zh: 他的画作质朴严肃，且刻意洋溢着一种罗马共和国早期高贵气度的感觉。

sentences.en: And again and again, his canvases are illustrating men who are prepared to devote their lives
sentences.zh: 他的画布一遍又一遍地描绘着那些随时准备奉献一生的人，

sentences.en: to their country, maybe even to sacrifice their own children in its cause, who put patriotism above all else.
sentences.zh: 为了他们的国家，甚至愿意为了国家的事业牺牲自己的亲生骨肉，他们将爱国主义置于一切之上。

sentences.en: And David is painting these even before the revolution breaks out.
sentences.zh: 而且大卫在大革命爆发之前就已经在创作这些画作了。

sentences.en: So when the revolution happens and people look at his paintings, it's as though David has already
sentences.zh: 因此，当大革命发生、人们看到他的画作时，就好像大卫在革命者们甚至还没开始行动之前，

sentences.en: been illustrating for the revolutionaries what they're doing before they had even begun to do it.
sentences.zh: 就已经在为他们描绘他们正在做的事了。

sentences.en: We've talked a little bit in this series, not enough for our American listeners.
sentences.zh: 我们在本系列中稍微讨论过这个，对我们的美国听众来说还不够。

sentences.en: We've talked about the influence of the American experiment.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过美国实验的影响。

sentences.en: So how much is this?
sentences.zh: 那么，这有多大程度是受其影响呢？

sentences.en: Because in America, people are already using that Roman model.
sentences.zh: 因为在美国，人们已经在运用那种罗马模式了。

sentences.en: Because really, if you've separated from Britain and you're going to be a Protestant
sentences.zh: 因为说实话，如果你已经脱离了英国，打算在大西洋岸边建立一个新教共和国，

sentences.en: Republic on the shores of the Atlantic, doing something that's never been done before, you've only got one historical analogy to grope for, which is the kind of classical world.
sentences.zh: 去做一件前所未有之事，你唯一能摸索的历史类比，就是古典世界那种类型。

sentences.en: So they're doing it in America.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在美洲这样做了。

sentences.en: Are people in France, do you think, actively copying that?
sentences.zh: 你认为法国的人们在积极地效仿吗？

sentences.en: Are they informed by that?
sentences.zh: 他们受其影响了吗？

sentences.en: There clearly are people in France who are very, very influenced by what is happening in America.
sentences.zh: 法国显然有些人深受美国正在发生的事情的影响。

sentences.en: Lafayette, your friend, would be an obvious example.
sentences.zh: 拉法耶特，你的朋友，就是一个明显的例子。

sentences.en: Big admirer of Lafayette, yeah.
sentences.zh: 拉法耶特的超级崇拜者，是的。

sentences.en: Jefferson is ambassador in that period.
sentences.zh: 杰斐逊在那期间担任大使。

sentences.en: Franklin had been a constant presence in Paris in the years before the revolution.
sentences.zh: 在大革命爆发前的几年里，富兰克林一直是巴黎的常客。

sentences.en: And there are certainly overt revolutionaries who are influenced by the example of the Americans.
sentences.zh: 而且确实有公开的革命者受到美国人榜样的影响。

sentences.en: But so too are even people, say, in the train of Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，甚至连玛丽·安托瓦内特身边的人也是如此，比如。

sentences.en: So the Princess de Lombard, who we'll be coming to in our next episode, she was a great admirer of Franklin.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们将会在下一集里讲到的朗巴尔亲王妃，她就是富兰克林的狂热崇拜者。

sentences.en: And she saw no contradiction between serving Marie Antoinette and being very close to her and admiring the founding fathers of America and the example of the American Republic.
sentences.zh: 她认为服务于玛丽·安托瓦内特并与她保持密切关系，与崇拜美国国父们以及美国共和国的榜样之间，并没有任何矛盾。

sentences.en: I think in Davide's case, there are huge shenanigans in his youth about whether he's going to get a scholarship to go to Rome and kind of feeling that he should have had it,
sentences.zh: 我认为在大卫的经历中，他年轻时为了能否获得去罗马的奖学金经历了一场极大的波折，并且总觉得他本该得到它，

sentences.en: but he's always being kind of frustrated in the chance to go.
sentences.zh: 但他去罗马的机会总是遭到各种挫折。

sentences.en: And so when he finally arrives there, it's the chance to Rome the eternal city is all the more precious to him.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他最终抵达那里时，前往永恒之城罗马的机会对他来说就更显珍贵。

sentences.en: I don't think that America stands between Davide and his imaginings of early Rome.
sentences.zh: 我不认为美国横亘在大卫与他早期罗马的幻想之间。

sentences.en: And I think that the look that you get in his paintings, which is kind of austere and lacking in any sense of kind of flummery and self-consciously antiquarian, I think this is
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你在他的画作中看到的风格——那种质朴、没有任何矫揉造作、并且刻意具有古玩气息的风格——我认为这是

sentences.en: his own.
sentences.zh: 他自己独有的。

sentences.en: And under the revolution, he brings this style to public display because people recognize that he's brilliant at the visuals.
sentences.zh: 在大革命期间，他将这种风格公之于众，因为人们认识到他在视觉表现上极其出色。

sentences.en: And as with so much else, in a revolutionary situation, people need a new look.
sentences.zh: 正如其他许多事情一样，在革命的局势中，人们需要一种崭新的面貌。

sentences.en: They need expressions of the revolution's identity that aren't drawing on what is being repudiated and rejected.
sentences.zh: 他们需要表达革命身份的呈现方式，而这些方式不能取材于那些正被唾弃和拒绝的事物。

sentences.en: And so he's the person who, for instance, is coordinating these great festivals that are being held on the Champs-de-Mars on Bastille Day.
sentences.zh: 所以他成为了那个在巴士底日协调在战神广场举行这些盛大节日庆典的人。

sentences.en: And of course, Davide entirely recognizes the Roman connotations of this, the Roman echoes of it.
sentences.zh: 当然，大卫完全意识到了其中蕴含的罗马内涵和罗马回响。

sentences.en: He's organizing when Voltaire's remains are brought to the Pantheon.
sentences.zh: 伏尔泰的遗骸被运往先贤祠时，是他负责组织的。

sentences.en: And the Pantheon is a great temple in Rome, built by Hadrian.
sentences.zh: 先贤祠是罗马的一座宏伟大神庙，由哈德良建造。

sentences.en: Oh, is it not?
sentences.zh: 哦，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of originally built by Gripper and then rebuilt by Hadrian.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它最初是由阿格里帕建造的，后来由哈德良重建。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But it's a very kind of Roman-looking building.
sentences.zh: 但它是一座非常具有罗马风格的建筑。

sentences.en: So again, it's a kind of classical ceremony.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，这是一种古典仪式。

sentences.en: And the Pantheon had originally been intended to be a church.
sentences.zh: 而先贤祠最初的建造目的是作为一座教堂。

sentences.en: So it's this, again, this idea of replacing Christianity with something that is Roman and revolutionary simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 所以，这又是这种用既是罗马的又是革命的事物来取代基督教的想法。

sentences.en: And Lynn Hunt, who's written a lot about this, is brilliant in all this.
sentences.zh: 林·亨特写了许多关于这方面的文章，在这方面她非常卓越。

sentences.en: I mean, she says there is no government without rituals and without symbols.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她说没有没有仪式和符号的政府。

sentences.en: You need rituals, you need symbols, and therefore you need people who are able to create and invent it.
sentences.zh: 你需要仪式，你需要符号，因此你需要能够创造和发明它们的人。

sentences.en: Sorry, you said replacing Christianity, but they're not overtly thinking about replacing
sentences.zh: 抱歉，你刚才说取代基督教，但他们此时此刻肯定没有公开考虑取代

sentences.en: Christianity at this point, surely.
sentences.zh: 基督教吧。

sentences.en: There is an anti-clerical tinge to it, but they're not thinking, you know, we are going to wipe away every last taint of...
sentences.zh: 其中带有一种反教权的色彩，但他们并没有在想，你知道的，我们要抹去……的每一丝痕迹。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, as we'll see when we do the next episode, hostility towards those priests who have refused to swear the oath of allegiance to the revolution, well, it's on the verge
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，正如我们在下一集里将看到的，对那些拒绝宣誓效忠革命的神职人员的敌意，简直

sentences.en: of becoming literally murderous.
sentences.zh: 快要发展到可以说是带有杀戮性的地步了。

sentences.en: And you talked yesterday about how legislation is brought in in the wake of the Tuileries forbidding even those priests who have sworn the oath to wear clerical garb in public.
sentences.zh: 你昨天谈到，杜伊勒里宫事件之后出台了一项立法，甚至禁止那些已经宣誓的神职人员在公共场合穿神职服装。

sentences.en: And so it's part of the climate of ideas, I think, that hostility to the priesthood inevitably spills into hostility towards Christianity itself.
sentences.zh: 所以这是思想气候的一部分，我认为，对神职人员的敌意不可避免地蔓延成了对基督教本身的敌意。

sentences.en: And the association of Christianity with reaction and superstition, throne and altar, it will come to be called, is becoming a very, very powerful, motivating factor.
sentences.zh: 基督教与反动、迷信、“王座与祭坛”（后来被称为这样）的联系，正在成为一个非常非常强大的推动因素。

sentences.en: And as the monarchy starts to totter, so also does the church.
sentences.zh: 随着君主制开始摇摇欲坠，教会也随之动摇。

sentences.en: It was initially the church that had sanctioned the anointing of kings, that had enshrined the monarchy as a kind of God-given gift from the Almighty.
sentences.zh: 最初是教会批准了国王的涂油加冕礼，将君主制尊为全能上帝赐予的礼物。

sentences.en: And so to contemplate destroying the monarchy is also to question the influence that the church has had and Christianity has had on centuries and centuries of French history.
sentences.zh: 因此，考虑摧毁君主制，也就是在质疑教会和基督教对数百年法国历史所产生的影响。

sentences.en: And so it becomes part of what is to be rejected.
sentences.zh: 所以这成了需要被唾弃的一部分。

sentences.en: And I think this is what is going on at this period.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是这一时期正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And so by rejecting the Ancien regime, rejecting Christianity, ancient Rome is the obvious place that you turn to.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过唾弃旧制度、唾弃基督教，古罗马就成了你理所当然转向的地方。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of people who still can't read.
sentences.zh: 所以当时还有很多人不识字。

sentences.en: So David's paintings, or reproductions of them, I guess, engravings and so on, must be very important in diffusing this kind of classical aesthetic.
sentences.zh: 因此，大卫的画作，或者它们的复制品，我猜比如版画等等，在传播这种古典美学方面一定非常重要。

sentences.en: But I read in your notes that there are also kind of souvenirs and things that people can buy.
sentences.zh: 但我在你的笔记里读到，当时还有人们可以购买的各种纪念品之类的小东西。

sentences.en: So brooches and stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如胸针之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you can buy brooches, which are stamped with the head of Brutus, and you can get pins
sentences.zh: 所以你可以买到印有布鲁图斯头像的胸针，还可以买到

sentences.en: in the form of the fasces, and the fasces are the rods that the lictors, who are the bodyguards
sentences.zh: 束棒形状的别针，束棒是罗马共和国选举产生的地方官的保镖——即利克托，

sentences.en: of elected magistrates in the Roman Republic, would carry in front and before the magistrate as he walked through the forum or whatever.
sentences.zh: 在长官走过广场或其它地方时，会走在长官前面并将其扛在身前的棍棒。

sentences.en: So people are literally dressing up as fascists.
sentences.zh: 所以人们实际上是在把自己装扮成法西斯分子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So for us, fasces have this kind of sinister connotation because they give the name to fascism.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，束棒带有这种阴险的内涵，因为法西斯主义就是因它而得名的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But you can see in the seats of government in Washington, D.C., the fasces are there.
sentences.zh: 但你可以在华盛顿特区的政府大楼里看到，束棒就在那里。

sentences.en: They're an inheritance from the American Revolution and the establishment of a Roman-type
sentences.zh: 它们是美国大革命以及在那里建立罗马式

sentences.en: republic there in exactly the way that the fasces are being used in the streets of revolutionary
sentences.zh: 共和国所传承下来的遗产，这与束棒在革命时期的巴黎街头被使用的方式

sentences.en: Paris.
sentences.zh: 完全一样。

sentences.en: Maybe that is an example of kind of an American influence, but again, I suspect not.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一种美国影响力的例子，但同样，我对此表示怀疑。

sentences.zh: 这兼具平民性、工人阶级性、革命性和罗马风范，因为那个细节——头发剪短且没有涂发粉。

sentences.en: Madame Tussaud's description, she specifies that this is a particular style, and it's called the Titus style.
sentences.zh: 杜莎夫人的描述中特意指出，这是一种特殊的风格，被称为“提图斯发型”。

sentences.en: And the name derives from the role of Titus in a play by Voltaire that he'd written several decades before.
sentences.zh: 这个名字源于伏尔泰在几十年写的一部戏剧中提图斯这个角色。

sentences.en: And this had been restaged in May 1791.
sentences.zh: 而这部戏在1791年5月重新上演了。

sentences.en: It's a great celebration of kind of Republican liberty and so on, and it had been played by
sentences.zh: 这是对共和主义自由等理念的一场盛大庆祝，当时是由

sentences.en: France's greatest actor.
sentences.zh: 法国最伟大的演员所扮演的。

sentences.en: And the name of this play is Brutus.
sentences.zh: 这部戏的名字叫《布鲁图斯》。

sentences.en: So this style of hair is simultaneously, it's what you wear in the slums, in the working class areas of Paris.
sentences.zh: 所以这种发型既是你走在巴黎贫民窟、工人阶级聚集区时会留的造型，

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But it's also what you wear if you want to affect a Roman look.
sentences.zh: 但它也是你想展现罗马风范时所留的发型。

sentences.en: And so this, I think, is why the Marseillais has the impact that it does, because it comes
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这就是为什么马赛人会产生那样的影响力，因为它恰好

sentences.en: at exactly this moment when the Roman and the working class are fusing in the broad culture of revolutionary Paris.
sentences.zh: 出现在罗马风范与工人阶级在革命巴黎的宏大文化中融合的这一时刻。

sentences.en: Paris, and they're arriving in their carmagnol, you know, these jackets that are kind of emblematic of the working classes.
sentences.zh: 巴黎，他们穿着卡马尼奥拉夹克到达——你知道的，这些夹克是工人阶级的象征。

sentences.en: When they come to Paris, the first areas that they go through are those that are very self-consciously working class, particularly the area around where the Bastille had stood.
sentences.zh: 当他们来到巴黎时，最先穿过的区域是那些具有强烈自觉意识的工人阶级区，尤其是巴斯蒂亚曾经矗立的地方周围的区域。

sentences.en: But they're singing a song that proclaims civic and martial virtue in a way that Romans might have done.
sentences.zh: 但他们唱着一首歌，以罗马人可能采用的方式宣扬着公民和尚武的美德。

sentences.en: And of course, as we said, they're then assembling on the Champs-de-Mars, the Campus Martius.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如我们所说，他们随后聚集在战神广场（Campus Martius）。

sentences.en: And you said how the Giraudet in due course will be intimidated by it and put off by it and parody it.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，吉伦特派日后会因此感到恐慌、畏惧并对其进行嘲讽。

sentences.en: Even at the time, of course, there are plenty of people in Paris who are terrified by this display, so royalists in particular.
sentences.zh: 即使在当时，巴黎也有大批人被这种阵势吓坏了，尤其是保王党人。

sentences.en: So there's an officer in the Royal Guards who sees them, the Marseillais, coming into Paris, singing this song.
sentences.zh: 因此，皇家卫队的一名军官看到他们——马赛人——唱着这首歌进入巴黎。

sentences.en: And he writes that they are 500 fanatics, three quarters of them drunk, followed by the dregs of the people.
sentences.zh: 他写道，他们是五百名狂热分子，其中四分之三喝醉了酒，后面跟着社会的残渣余孽。

sentences.en: But of course, Dominic, there writes a man who is on the wrong side of history.
sentences.zh: 但当然了，多米尼克，那里写下这些的是一个站在历史错误一边的人。

sentences.en: So the wrong side of history, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以是站在历史错误的一边，汤姆。

sentences.en: So there you've got an unnamed officer in the Royal Guards, a man of sense and discretion.
sentences.zh: 所以你在那里看到的是皇家卫队的一名匿名军官，一个理智且谨慎的人。

sentences.en: He and I on the wrong side of history.
sentences.zh: 他和我都站在历史错误的一边。

sentences.en: Tom, you're on the right side of history, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你站在历史正确的一边，对吧？

sentences.en: Do-gooder with Theo, our producer.
sentences.zh: 和我们的制作人蒂奥一起做慈善的好人。

sentences.en: You're dressed in your street garb.
sentences.zh: 你穿着你的街头行头。

sentences.en: I love a Roman, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我真喜欢罗马人，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I look at you now in your street garb with your Roman haircut, shocking scenes.
sentences.zh: 我现在看着你穿着街头行头，留着罗马发型，真是令人震惊的场面。

sentences.en: So everybody knows where we stand.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都知道我们的立场。

sentences.en: So our plan was originally to get to the execution of the king, and we've obviously completely failed to do that because there is just too much drama.
sentences.zh: 所以我们原本的计划是讲到处决国王，而我们显然彻底失败了，因为这里面的戏剧性实在太丰富了。

sentences.en: So what we're going to do is we're going to bring down the curtain on season two of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要做的，是为法国大革命第二季落下帷幕。

sentences.en: But the good news is that we will be back in the spring with season three, and that will be more exciting than ever.
sentences.zh: 但好消息是，我们将在春季带着第三季回归，那将会比以往更加精彩。

sentences.en: We will get into the September massacres, to the fall of the monarchy, to the rapidly changing
sentences.zh: 我们将深入探讨九月大屠杀、君主制的覆灭、

sentences.en: fortunes on the battlefield, and most excitingly, to the trial and execution of Louis XVI.
sentences.zh: 战场上瞬息万变的局势，以及最令人兴奋的——路易十六的审判与处决。

sentences.en: But next week, we will be changing focus completely because we will be in America in 1968 for the fall of Lyndon Johnson,
sentences.zh: 但下周，我们将彻底转换焦点，因为我们将前往1968年的美国，聚焦林登·约翰逊的下台、

sentences.en: the assassinations of Martin Luther King and Robert Kennedy, and in the long run, the great comeback of Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金和罗伯特·肯尼迪的遇刺，以及从长远来看理查德·尼克松的伟大回归。

sentences.en: And the good news for members of the Rest is History Club, you will get access to the entire America in 1968 series, all six episodes on Monday.
sentences.zh: 对于“历史其余部分”俱乐部（The Rest is History Club）的会员来说有个好消息，你将在周一获得整个1968年美国系列的所有六集内容。

sentences.en: And of course, if you want to join the Rest is History Club and sign up, you just have to go to therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你想加入“历史其余部分”俱乐部并进行注册，你只需访问 therestishistory.com。

sentences.en: So on that bombshell, merci Tom, that was magnifique, and à bientôt, everybody.
sentences.zh: 带着这个爆炸性的消息，谢谢汤姆，这太精彩了，大家再见（à bientôt）。

sentences.en: Au revoir.
sentences.zh: 再见（Au revoir）。

sentences.zh: 回头见（À bientôt）。
